public_rationale: The evidence is consistent with Marcus’s claim, but does not establish its majority threshold. February reporting describes financing still under negotiation, and SoftBank confirms that equity allocations remained unsettled. Neither gives a complete secured-funding total or a reliable upper bound. OpenAI’s earlier announcement of an initial $100 billion deployment also cannot be treated as a statement that this was all the funding available. On this record, concluding that no more than $250 billion was secured would require an additional inference.
limitations: Private financing arrangements may not have been publicly disclosed.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI and partners do not have all or most of the Stargate funding in hand.

statement.excerpt: (And Elon is right that they don’t have all or most of the Stargate funding in hand).

our_interpretation: The plain reading is that OpenAI and its partners had not secured a majority of Stargate’s announced $500 billion funding.
Most means more than half. Support therefore requires evidence that no more than $250 billion was secured.
In hand includes cash obtained and binding financing available to the project. It excludes fundraising ambitions and financing still under discussion.

Because this describes an ongoing state without a reporting period, use February 2025, the latest completed calendar month before publication. Stargate funding is an event-driven financing measure rather than a regularly reported quarterly account.
Treat the attributed outside assessment of funding as an estimate, rather than a claim based on audited company accounts.
This does not assert that Stargate would fail to raise money later or that the entire four-year budget needed to be available immediately.
criteria.support_condition: Reliable records or reporting establish that no more than $250 billion of the announced $500 billion was secured during the target period.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable records or reporting establish that more than $250 billion of the announced $500 billion was secured during the target period.

evidence.explanation: The announcement distinguishes a $500 billion four-year investment intention from an initial $100 billion deployment. It cautions against assuming no funding existed, but neither supplies a February secured-funding total nor demonstrates that a majority was available.
